challenges.name: earnings-today-fix
challenges.title: Fix the earnings card
challenges.description: The courier app's "Today" card was wrong twice a week: deliveries made after 17:00 counted into the next day on phones set to UTC, the unit tests passed or failed depending on the hour CI ran them, and a delivery stamped exactly at midnight showed up in both days. The calculator now receives its data source and a `java.time.Clock` through its constructor, and the editor holds `EarningsCalculator.kt` with the old date logic cut out, each block marked by a `// [ ]` line; some pieces are the old, buggy code. Fill every line so that: today is the date of the injected clock in the business time zone `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`, never the phone's zone or the real time; the day runs from local midnight to the next local midnight, end excluded; and only `DELIVERED` orders inside that window count (fee + tip). The runner gives the calculator a fixed clock whose own zone is UTC and a fake source that returns every delivery it holds, and prints the day, its start instant, the count and the total.
hints: Write down the instants: 23:40 in Ho Chi Minh City is 16:40Z. Which date is that for the courier, which instant does their day start at, and which pieces would give a different answer on a phone or a CI machine set to UTC?
Look at `LocalDate.now(clock)` with `clock.withZone(...)`, `LocalDate.atStartOfDay(zone)`, and `Instant.isBefore` for a half-open window `[start, end)`.

A store that closes its till at local midnight in Tokyo, tested with `Clock.fixed(Instant.parse("2026-05-01T15:30:00Z"), ZoneOffset.UTC)`: `val d = LocalDate.now(clock.withZone(ZoneId.of("Asia/Tokyo")))` gives 2026-05-02, `d.atStartOfDay(ZoneId.of("Asia/Tokyo")).toInstant()` gives 2026-05-01T15:00:00Z, and a sale counts when `!at.isBefore(start) && at.isBefore(end)`.

tests.name: Midday: today's delivered orders count, cancelled and yesterday's do not

delivery d2 2026-03-13T17:05:00Z 15000 0 DELIVERED
delivery d3 2026-03-13T16:55:00Z 20000 0 DELIVERED
